source.title: Cross-Modal Attention Guided Unlearning in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Karuna Bhaila; Aneesh Komanduri; Minh-Hao Van; Xin-Tao Wu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests unlearning and paraphrased-prompt extraction in a new modality and setting: VQA on vision-language models with synthetic biographical data.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning metrics and Adversarial Privacy Extraction (APE), which tests paraphrased queries against unlearned models. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. The cited result about performance using 5% of image tokens is prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study reports forget-set accuracy, general VQA accuracy and a paraphrase-extraction attack (APE) for several unlearning methods on two VLMs (FIUBench). This is a new setting bearing on A and E, and on F for its own method CAGUL against paraphrase attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude CAGUL gives favorable forget/retain/efficiency trade-offs with a frozen VLM and resists rephrased queries on LLaMA. On Qwen they concede weaker forgetting and a decline in non-private (Dnp) metrics, attributed to architecture.
record.recipe_differences: This is a new VLM method, not a reproduction of the cited LLM methods: it freezes the pretrained VLM and trains an image discriminator and visual-token encoder, using PO+GD objectives and attention-guided token transformations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model architecture and unlearning method. The study also varies the number of transformed tokens and forget-set size; it reports that CAGUL's best forget and retain metrics occur at k=200 and that performance generally remains similar across tested k values.

fits_no_version.finding: CAGUL keeps all VLM weights frozen and gates forgetting through an image discriminator plus a token encoder. Without the encoder, Df EM is 37.75 and APE 23.67 (Table 5), so the knowledge remains intact in the weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-gating unlearning blocks access by design; the knowledge would be recovered if the discriminator is bypassed or misclassifies an image.

record.problems: Experiments report performance over a single run. Evaluation uses two VLMs and a synthetic fictitious-biography dataset. No chance-level threshold is supplied for the reported EM metric.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for Rouge-L, MinK, retain-set measures, efficiency, and CAGUL ablations are omitted because they do not directly measure targeted-knowledge recovery under the listed claim versions. Results for varying k and forget-set size are also omitted because they report CAGUL setting trends, not recovery attacks.

untested.parts: No activation-direction ablation or deletion-vs-blocking analysis of unlearned weights.
Only paraphrased queries (APE); no jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information.
CAGUL is tested only against paraphrase extraction; no fine-tuning, internal-edit or quantization attacks, and no attack that bypasses its discriminator.
Only paraphrase attacks are tested as the simple attack.

missing.what: Retain-set metrics: Qwen GA+KL Dr Rouge 8.66 and Dnp EM 0.79; Qwen CAGUL Dnp EM 40.01 vs Finetune 53.51. These are the utility costs bearing on A.
Ablation without the encoder: EM 37.75, APE 23.67. This shows the frozen base model retains the knowledge.
MinK membership-inference scores for forget sets (e.g. CAGUL-LLaMA 14.86 vs Finetune 43.32).

record.verdict_notes: Reader version codes V1/V5/V6 map to A/E/F. For E, the Finetune baseline is misleading: recovery should be judged against each method's own Df EM. APE is never above it, so the Qwen 'partial' values reflect incomplete unlearning, not paraphrase recovery. LLaMA's Finetune general accuracy (MME 30.58) is already far below Pretrain (77.34), so 'keeping general ability' means keeping the finetuned level. Single run, synthetic data, two VLMs. The 5%-image-token result is cited prior work.

versions.untested_parts: No explicit chance-level threshold is stated; the study evaluates VQA forgetting metrics and downstream accuracy, but not general ability across all tasks.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether the unlearning method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests paraphrased queries through APE only; no separate tests of jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
CAGUL is evaluated against paraphrased-query extraction only, not fine-tuning recovery, internal edits, quantization, or the other prompting attacks listed in the claim.

relation.reason: Reports forgetting, utility and paraphrase-attack results bearing on A, E and F.

tranche.reason: New VLM setting (FIUBench), with forget, retain, general-ability and paraphrase-attack results for several unlearning methods.

source_check.notes: All 25 values match Tables 3 and 6. Single run, no uncertainty; LoRA baselines, GA-loss methods early-stopped. CAGUL leaves weights frozen, so the knowledge stays in the model behind an image discriminator. APE changes only the text. Retrain Df EM is 15.75 (LLaMA) and 14.52 (Qwen). Finetune already cut MME far below Pretrain (77.34 to 30.58).

statements.correction: CAGUL (frozen VLM, trained image discriminator and visual-token encoder, PO+GD losses) on Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct, FIUBench, 40 persons' health/criminal queries: Df EM 39.68 to 1.70 (Retrain 15.75, Pretrain 0.00). Paraphrase APE 24.59 to 0.43. MME 30.58 and POPE 37.70 equal Finetune. Preprint, single run, no uncertainty, no code.
statements.problem: Cites r06 but gives no result for 2510.07567. Its 'why' covers only CUSE, SafeEraser, HFRU and PPE-Bench. What it says about other studies is not wrong for this one, but this study's contribution is missing.

statements.correction: Qwen-2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, GA (LoRA, early stopping), FIUBench health/criminal queries: Df EM 56.92 to 0.18. Retain-set Rouge 72.49 to 0.04 and Dnp EM 53.51 to 0.00, so outputs collapse. MME 67.58 to 28.99, POPE 79.24 to 45.74. Single run.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. But the differences list 'OFFSIDE uses LoRA' as a difference, and this study's GA is LoRA too, with early stopping. The EM drop also comes with collapsed outputs, so it is not targeted forgetting.

statements.correction: APE is the average EM over several paraphrases per forget sample (Ma et al. 2025). It is at or below each method's own Df EM on both models.
statements.problem: Minor: APE equals EM for Qwen GA (0.18). Finetune APE is already below its EM (24.59 vs 39.68; 45.62 vs 56.92), so APE at or below EM partly reflects the paraphrase penalty itself. This text does not give the paraphrase source.

statements.correction: CAGUL (the authors' own method) on Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct (11B), FIUBench: paraphrase APE 0.43 vs its own Df EM 1.70 (Finetune APE 24.59, Pretrain 0.00). Preprint, no code, single run, no uncertainty.
statements.problem: Cites r18 but names only four other methods ('All four are preprints'). Its conditions, '3B-9B vision-language models', exclude this study's 11B model.

statements.problem: Cites r12 and r24 but never names the study, and its conditions omit FIUBench. The row fits the thesis, since paraphrase resistance comes with incomplete forgetting. 'Barely removed' overstates it: EM fell by 35%.

statements.correction: CAGUL Df EM 1.70 on Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct vs 37.13 on Qwen-2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. APE 0.43 vs 23.78, below each model's own EM. Settings differ: k=200 of 6404 visual tokens on LLaMA, k=20 of 1369 on Qwen.
statements.problem: Cites r06 and r12 but never names the study. These rows show that how much CAGUL forgets depends on the backbone. Its paraphrase resistance (APE at or below EM) holds on both models. The conditions list no VLMs.
